_meta.description: Single source of truth for the BrawlApex Intelligence Engine. Encodes Bobby's draft framework ('The Best Draft Guide EVER' parts 1+2): the 7 draft classes, the counter triangle (Control > Anti-Tank > Tank/Aggro > Control), active vs passive mode tempo, thrower rules, space-maker timing, and 1-mid + 2-lane team structure. Read by src/data/draftEngine.js (browser) AND scrapers/meta_weights.py (daily intelligence refresh) — edit here, both sides follow.

rankedIneligible._comment: Manually maintained hard-exclusion list — brawlers newly released but not yet legal in competitive Ranked. Belt-and-suspenders on top of the scraper's ranked-only filter (scrapers/common.py): if a brawler's data ever leaks in anyway (mistagged battle type, a spidered match from before their ranked debut), this keeps them out of suggestions and the blind-pick list regardless. getDraftAdvice excludes every key listed here from its candidate pool entirely. Remove a brawler from this list the patch they go live in Ranked.

brawlerClassOverrides._comment: Owner-confirmed draft class for every brawler, transcribed from Bobby's role map (screenshot 2026-07-17). Always wins over apiClassToDraftClass — draftClassOf() checks this first regardless of the brawler's official Supercell class, so it's the single source of truth for the draft engine's class assignment, not just a patch for Unknown-class new releases.

abilityLabels._comment: Ability tags from the same role map — a static per-brawler trait shown as a badge on suggestion cards, distinct from data-driven flags like Meta Breaker. A value may be a single tag OR an array when a brawler genuinely carries two (RUFFS breaks walls via his star power on top of being a Good Hyper); every rule reads the full array, while the card badge shows the first entry, so list the draft-relevant tag first.

brawlerAbilities._comment: Ability tags. A value is a single tag or an ARRAY when a brawler carries several; every rule reads the full array via abilitiesOf, while the card badge shows the FIRST entry, so the draft-relevant tag is listed first. REBUILT 2026-08-31 after the owner found Gale, Cordelius and Spike tagged WALL_BREAK when none of them break walls. The old table was a one-tag-per-brawler taxonomy - 104 of 105 carried exactly one tag from five mutually exclusive buckets - so a bucket NAMED wall break was standing in for an ability list, and it was wrong in both directions: seven tagged brawlers did not break walls, while twelve that do (Shelly, Dynamike, Bull, El Primo, Gene, Grom, Chester, Pearl, Piper and more) were locked out because their slot was already spent. WALL_BREAK now means the SUPER or attack breaks walls every cycle (12 brawlers). WALL_BREAK_COND means it is gated behind a gadget, star power or hyper (7), which depends on a build we cannot observe from the draft - abilityRules.conditionalWeight prices that gap. WALL_CREATE (Sprout) and BUSH_CREATE (Rosa) are the inverse mechanics and had no representation at all; they shift map geometry the other way. Owner-sourced, 2026-08-31.

counterMatrix._comment: counterMatrix[A][B] > 0 means class A beats class B, IN WIN-RATE POINTS. MEASURED 2026-08-29 over 250,000 Masters matches, replacing the hand-authored -2..+2 table. Four things make it trustworthy, and all four are load-bearing if you ever rebuild it. (1) SOLO STRENGTH IS REMOVED with a coefficient FITTED (1.004), not assumed - solo win rate alone explains 64% of head-to-head edge, so an unadjusted matrix mostly learns which classes hold strong brawlers, which soloWR already scores. An earlier pass assumed 0.5 and the leftover strength produced two confident false findings: that Anti-Tank does NOT beat Tank, and that Ash/Bolt are a separate archetype. Both dissolve at the fitted value - Ash and Bolt are ordinary tanks (matchup residual +0.18 and -0.16) that are simply strong. (2) MAP CONTROL: each cell is pooled WITHIN maps, because two classes are drafted onto different maps and the raw cross-tab confuses that selection with a matchup. This is not cosmetic - Tank vs Thrower reads +0.52 raw and -0.05 map-controlled. (3) SHRINKAGE: every cell is shrunk toward 0 by its own standard error (empirical Bayes; across the 42 cells the observed sd is 0.86 pts of which 0.21 is noise). Thin cells therefore cannot assert a matchup the sample will not carry, which is the same priors-vs-evidence rule the rest of the engine obeys. (4) EXACTLY ANTISYMMETRIC, M[a][b] = -M[b][a] - see the invariant in CLAUDE.md. WHAT IT FOUND: Bobby's triangle largely survives. Anti-Tank does beat Tank (+1.06, not the claimed +2.00) and Space Maker does dive backline (+2.06 vs Thrower, +1.12 vs Sniper). Anti-Tank loses to Thrower (-1.71), as authored. The genuine corrections are both in the Tank row: tanks were said to lose 1.5 to throwers and that is NOT TRUE and NOT REVERSED EITHER - it is 0.00, a wash, the single largest false claim in the old table; and tanks were said to lose 1.0 to snipers when they in fact beat them (+0.60, which does clear its error bar). Do not read a class cell as a duel: it is a TEAM-level outcome for comps containing those classes, and within-class spread is huge - vs throwers, Bolt is +5.79 and Buster -5.19 around a class mean of zero. Per-brawler truth lives in vs_brawler, not here. Held out over 23,772 real pick decisions, swapping these values in moved AUC by +0.0002 +/-0.0013 - nothing. It ships to make the 'Counters X' / 'Weak vs Y' chips TRUE, not to predict better.

matchupOverrides._comment: Per-brawler exceptions to the class counter matrix, in the same WIN-RATE POINT units. Value = the LISTED brawler's edge against that enemy class, replacing its class default in BOTH directions (the reverse pairing uses the negation). Currently EMPTY. It held one entry, BOLT/THROWER = 0, whose job was to cancel the authored matrix's false claim that tanks lose 1.5 to throwers. The measured matrix has no such claim (Tank vs Thrower is +0.63), so the override became a penalty rather than a relief: Bolt measures +4.59 vs throwers over ~1,000 pairing-games, and pinning him to 0 would understate him. Not re-encoded at the measured value on purpose - one brawler on a four-figure sample is a thin basis for a hand-entry, and vs_brawler already carries Bolt's real per-enemy edges with proper shrinkage. Add an entry here only for an exception that vs_brawler cannot see, and damp it like any other prior.

synergyPairs._comment: SUPERSEDED by duoSynergy, which measures real brawler pairs from with_brawler. Kept only as the fallback when a duo has no measured sample. As authored this table could not move anything: 8 of 28 class pairs carry a value, all positive so both teams collect some, and the differential is exactly zero in 27.5% of real drafts. Removing it changed the verdict's AUC by 0.0000.

roles._comment: Standard ranked structure: one mid (objective player) + two laners. Lane anchors can hold a lane 1v1; objective specialists carry the mode's win condition.
roles._perModeNote: midClassesByMode / laneAnchorClassesByMode override the flat lists for one mode; an EMPTY list means the mode has no such requirement, so the check always passes and the role contributes no points either way (same convention objectiveSpecialistByMode already used for a mode with no entry). Both overrides are measured, discordant-pair, on 1.5M Masters matches - counting only games where exactly one side satisfied the rule, which controls for map and opponent because both sides played the same game. HAVING A LANE ANCHOR is worth +2.59 +/- 0.46 in five modes but -3.11 +/- 0.85 in HEIST, a clean reversal: heist wants a space maker on the safe, not a laner holding a side. HAVING A MID is worth +2.20 in brawlBall and +2.45 in gemGrab but -0.56 +/- 0.38 in bounty and -0.08 +/- 0.43 in knockout, so the requirement is real in the two objective modes and absent in the two elimination modes. Both rules bind rarely - the anchor check on 2-6%% of matches, the mid check on 6-32%% - which is why they were never noticed.
roles._objectiveNote: Measured 2026-08-31, discordant pairs over 1.5M Masters matches: the win-rate lift of holding at least one of a class, counting only games where exactly one side did. Three memberships were wrong and are corrected here. brawlBall dropped SPACE_MAKER (-0.52) and keeps TANK (+3.04) - the ball carrier role in brawl ball is carried entirely by tanks, and space makers measure slightly negative there while the rule paid them +4. heist dropped TANK (-1.06) and keeps SPACE_MAKER (+6.02, the largest lift anywhere in the table) and ANTI_TANK (+1.44). gemGrab dropped SUPPORT (-0.27) and gained TANK (+2.01), which was the mode's best class and was missing. Unchanged and confirmed: hotZone CONTROL +0.79 / TANK +2.76, knockout SNIPER +1.61 / THROWER +0.60, bounty SNIPER +2.06 (the mode's best). NOTE the flat `fixed * 4` in getDraftAdvice is still a single constant standing in for lifts that range -1.1 to +6.0; membership is now right, magnitude is not.

modes._comment: Bobby's two metas: active/aggro (Brawl Ball, Gem Grab, Hot Zone, Heist) vs passive (Bounty, Knockout). classWeights scale a brawler's score on that mode; maxPerClass enforces e.g. 'in Brawl Ball limit control to one brawler maximum'. damageOverMatchup relaxes matchup penalties where raw output wins ('I'd much rather have bad matchups with good damage' — Heist).

statisticalCoefficients._comment: Applied by meta_weights.py when building brawler_intelligence, and by the engine as score multipliers. true_win_rate = Bayesian shrink of raw WR toward 50% with confidencePriorGames of prior weight, so tiny samples can't fake a 60% brawler.

recency._comment: Dual-window drift detection: brawler_intelligence carries recent_* stats over the last windowDays (computed from collected_at). When the recent sample is solid, the engine blends recent WR at recentWeight over the full-patch rate — so a shadow nerf shows up in suggestions within days, no matter how many older games say otherwise. trendDeltaPct is the recent-vs-overall gap that surfaces a trending chip.

statisticalCoefficients._flagNote: All three scoreMultipliers were set to 1.0 on 2026-08-31 after being measured. They still SET THEIR CHIPS - the label is information the card should carry - but they no longer move the score, because two of them cannot fire at all and the third predicts nothing. popularityTrap needs >=20%% pick rate AND <=48%% win rate: of 105 brawlers, ZERO qualify, because the five above 20%% (Max 28.2/49.7, Griff 26.6/50.4, Stu 24.7/52.1, Brock 24.5/51.3, Rico 22.9/52.4) are all above 49.7%%. inflationBias needs <=3%% pick AND >=55%% WR: also ZERO, because the only two brawlers over 55%% are Ash (7.7%% picked) and Bolt (5.2%%), both far above the gate. brokenIndicator fires for three (Stu, Rico, Emz) and paid them +6 points on the claim that they are stronger than their win rate shows - splitting the collection window in half, their win rates moved +0.56, -0.27 and +0.01, i.e. flat. Retune the THRESHOLDS if you want these back; the multipliers were never the problem.

throwerPenalty._comment: Bobby: 'never pick a thrower unless it's last pick or you have protection for it'. Penalty in win-rate points, waived outright if the team already fields a protection class, halved in passive-tempo modes where throwers are structurally strong, and scaled by slot via slotMultipliers.
throwerPenalty._slotNote: The penalty used to LIFT ENTIRELY at slot 5 (the slot list was 1-4), and that was too sharp a cliff: an unprotected thrower went from -14 to 0 in one pick, which is a large part of why throwers cluster at the top of pick-5 lists. Owner decision 2026-08-30: at pick 5 the penalty is REDUCED, not lifted. 0.35 is not a fit - it is the residual counter-draft share, because the rule bundles two risks that resolve at different times. PROTECTION is fully resolved by slot 5: in the 1-2-2-1 order blue holds slots 1/4/5, so slot 5 is blue's last pick and no frontline is coming that the waivedWithProtection check has not already seen. COUNTER-DRAFT is not: the enemy still holds slot 6, which is enemyPicksRemaining/3 = 1/3 of the risk the rule prices at slot 1 - the same shape counterability and the thin-map term already use. Slot 6 stays at 0 because there both risks are genuinely over, which is Bobby's pick-6 out and what throwerLastPick's bonus is for. At -14 x 0.35 = -4.9 the slot-5 term sits alongside counter-stack (+4) and anti-tank (+4) rather than dwarfing the measured head-to-head and duo terms, which is what the scale contract requires. NOTE this deliberately breaks the slot list's long-standing tie to mapPriority.presenceFloor - the floor still lifts entirely at 5 and 6.

classDiversity._comment: Bobby: 'if you pick three control brawlers, all of your brawlers are countered by one aggro'. Multiplier per duplicate class already on the team (compounds: 0.7, then 0.49).
classDiversity._reliefComment: The stacking penalty exists because a stacked comp invites ONE counter-pick that answers all of it — a counter-DRAFT risk. Once the enemy has no picks left that risk is gone, so the penalty is relieved by this fraction (1 = fully neutral) when enemyPicksRemaining is 0. This is not a free pass: being countered by the enemy's ALREADY-REVEALED picks is priced separately by the PASS 2 counter matrix, and a structurally broken comp (no mid / no lane anchor / no objective specialist) is still caught by finalSanityCheck. Owner-confirmed 2026-07-25: 'it is fine to stack if there are no more picks and they cant be countered.'

antiTankFirstPick._comment: Bobby: 'anti-tank is the foundation of every draft'; best anti-tank is almost always the correct first pick in objective (active) modes.

spaceMakerLateBonus._comment: Space makers are the skill separator — strongest in slots 4-6 when the enemy comp is revealed and can't answer the dive.

counterStack._comment: Bobby: 'if the enemy commits to a class, the hard counter to it is almost a free pick'. When the enemy fields 2+ of one class, a brawler whose class hard-counters it (counterMatrix >= hardCounterThreshold) gets a flat bonus PER stacked enemy - applied AFTER mode weighting so a favorable enemy mode can't bury the counter (e.g. two snipers on a Bounty map still make Mortis/Kit a lock). Threshold 1.5 -> 1.0 on 2026-08-29: it is read against counterMatrix, which now carries MEASURED win-rate points (RMS 0.88, max 2.15) instead of authored -2..+2 units (RMS 1.21). At 1.5 only two of the 42 class pairings would ever have qualified and the rule would have gone effectively dead. 1.0 is 'a full win-rate point of class edge' and keeps roughly the set of pairings the rule was written to fire on.
counterStack._measuredNote: bonusPerEnemy 4 -> 1.75 on 2026-08-31. The rule is REAL - all six qualifying matrix pairings measure positive when the opponent has stacked 2+ of a class: SPACE_MAKER into 2 throwers +11.75 +/- 2.9, ANTI_TANK into 2 tanks +4.77 +/- 1.2, TANK into 2 controls +3.62 +/- 0.6, TANK into 2 space makers +3.53 +/- 0.5, SPACE_MAKER into 2 snipers +1.87 +/- 0.5, THROWER into 2 anti-tanks +1.22 +/- 0.4. But at 4 PER ENEMY the rule paid +8 at a stack of two against a mean measured lift near +3.5. The spread (1.2 to 11.8) is also far wider than one constant can carry - reading the per-pair value off counterMatrix would be the better fix.

abilityRules._comment: Ability-tag synergy/counter rules (Bobby): wall break opens lanes for snipers, strips the cover throwers depend on, and forces anti-tanks into the open where snipers kite them. Bonuses are additive win-rate points on the ~50-point score base, per the scoring scale contract.
abilityRules._conditionalNote: What a WALL_BREAK_COND tag is worth relative to a full WALL_BREAK. A super that breaks walls fires every cycle; a gadget, star power or hyper break depends on a build we cannot observe from the draft, and the opponent may simply not have it equipped. 0.5 is a PRIOR, not a fit - there is no way to measure equipped builds from ranked_matches. It scales every wall-break bonus and the thrower-window gate. Geometry deliberately ignores conditional breakers entirely: re-reading a whole map's openness is too large a consequence for an ability that may never appear.
abilityRules._remeasuredNote: RESTORED 2026-08-31 at measured values, after the tag rebuild. Every figure is a 2x2 interaction over 3.0M Masters sides using the CORRECTED 12-brawler super cohort - (win rate with the ability AND the condition, minus with the condition alone) minus the same difference without the condition. wallBreakSniperSynergy 4 -> 1.0 (measured +1.07 +/- 0.24 over 246,583 sides). wallBreakVsThrower 7 -> 0.65 (+0.65 +/- 0.34 over 102,521); the same interaction read from the thrower's side is -0.65, as it must be. wallBreakSniperVsAntiTank 4 -> 0 (measured -0.22 +/- 0.33, indistinguishable from zero). sniperWithWallBreakSynergy 3 -> 1.0, the mirror of the first rule. CORRECTING THE TAGS CHANGED THE ANSWERS: on the old broken cohort the sniper rule read +1.13 and the own-thrower rule read +1.61 (backwards); with real wall-breakers the own-thrower penalty comes out -1.04, so the shipped DIRECTION was right all along and only the magnitude was wrong. One confound had to be removed by hand: BROCK and PIPER are both wall-breakers AND snipers, so 'my team has a wall breaker' and 'my team has a sniper' are the same fact whenever either is present - that alone inflated the sniper synergy from +1.07 to +2.97. Any future measurement of a team-composition rule has to check for members that satisfy both sides. The CONDITIONAL cohort measures -0.81 against throwers, i.e. no benefit at all, which argues conditionalWeight should be below 0.5; it is left there because that cohort is a different set of brawlers and the reading is confounded. OLD NOTE, kept for the record: all four rules were zeroed
abilityRules._defectHistory: ALL FOUR RULES WERE ZEROED as of 2026-08-31 because the tag they key on is wrong, NOT because the mechanic is wrong. brawlerAbilities is not an ability list: 104 of 105 brawlers carry exactly ONE tag from five mutually exclusive buckets (SPECIAL 40, GOOD_HYPER 30, PIERCE_DAMAGE 13, KNOCKBACK_STUN 12, WALL_BREAK 10), so it is a primary-trait taxonomy that happens to have a bucket NAMED wall break. The set it produces is wrong in both directions - owner-confirmed that GALE, CORDELIUS and SPIKE do not break walls, and the same goes for GRAY, GRIFF, FRANK and STU, while SHELLY, DYNAMIKE and BULL genuinely do break walls and are tagged KNOCKBACK_STUN or GOOD_HYPER so they can never trigger these rules. Four of the ten tagged are among the most-played brawlers in the game (Griff 26.6%%, Stu 24.7%%, Brock 24.5%%, Colt), so the rules fired constantly on a false premise, and wallBreakVsThrower at +7 was the single largest constant in the config. A 2x2 interaction over 3.0M sides put that cohort at +0.25 for the thrower rule and +1.13 for the sniper rule, but those numbers describe an arbitrary group and MUST NOT be used to retune these constants. THE FIX IS THE DATA: give brawlerAbilities a real multi-tag ability list (Ruffs already shows the array form works), then re-measure and restore values. Until then these contribute nothing, which is the honest state. The same defect disables geometry.wallBreakShiftsOpen, attributeRules.wallBreakOwnThrower, mapRules[].wallBreakBonus and the requiresEnemyNoWallBreak gate on counterLadder.throwerLastPick - that gate now passes almost always, making the thrower window more permissive than intended.

wallBreakSniperVsAntiTank._zeroNote: Measured -0.22 +/- 0.33 over 111,245 sides - zero. Kept at 0 rather than deleted so the rule and its chip survive if the map pool ever makes it true.
wallBreakSniperVsAntiTank.label: Forces anti-tank open

supportRules._comment: Bobby: supports are reactive 'conditional modifiers'. Never draft one in the first two global picks unless it's a meta-anchor on this map (waiver: map true WR >= waiverMinMapTrueWR); never without a lane/aggro partner to support. Named combos reward the known pairings late-draft.
supportRules._noPartnerNote: Was -6 until 2026-08-31, when it was measured and found to have the WRONG SIGN. Across 604,012 sides holding a support, those WITH one of needsPartnerClasses won 50.06%% and those WITHOUT won 50.38%% - the penalty fired on the teams that did slightly better (+0.32 +/- 0.61, i.e. indistinguishable from zero either way). It also binds rarely: only 27,425 support sides, 4.5%%, lack a partner at all. Set to 0 rather than deleted so the chip and the structure survive if a real effect ever shows up.

combos._note: Mode gate removed 2026-08-31. The effect is real - Kit with a tank or space maker beats Kit without one by +3.37 +/- 1.78 in knockout - but it is just as strong in bounty at +3.46 +/- 2.05, so restricting it to knockout was hiding half of it. Bonus 6 -> 3.4, the measured value.
combos.label: Kit ride-along

combos._note: Tempo gate INVERTED 2026-08-31 - it was passive, and passive is exactly where the effect does not exist. Max's win rate with an enemy sniper on the board, minus without: knockout -0.39 +/- 0.77 and bounty -0.34 +/- 0.73, the two passive modes where the rule used to fire, both indistinguishable from zero. The four ACTIVE modes are where it lives: hotZone +7.32 +/- 1.04, heist +6.74 +/- 1.27, gemGrab +5.78 +/- 0.97, brawlBall +2.96. The reading is that running a sniper down is worth something when there is an objective forcing the fight, and worth nothing in an elimination mode where the sniper can simply hold range. Bonus kept at 5, which sits inside the active-mode range.
combos.label: Runs down snipers

combos._note: Bonus 3 -> 0 on 2026-08-31, kept only as a record. Max in brawl ball measures 50.80%% against his own 49.68%% global, so the claim is directionally true - but that +1.12 is already the score base, which blends his map rate toward his MODE rate. A flat mode bonus on top is a second copy of the same fact, the same double count that emptied brawlerBias. A combo entry should encode an INTERACTION the base cannot see (Kit needing a frontline, Max needing an enemy sniper), never a brawler simply being good in a mode.
combos.label: Tempo engine

counterLadder._comment: Phase-specific drafting: picks 1-2 are the anchor phase (stats-led, counters barely matter — the enemy hasn't committed), 3-4 target revealed picks, 5-6 are hard-counter execution. counterWeightBySlot scales BOTH the class-matrix and empirical vs-class edges. Preventative blocking (PASS 3) is naturally off at slot 6 since the enemy comp is complete. lastPickSpecialist: a brawler with a thin map sample is demoted at every slot. throwerLastPick: at slots 5-6 a thrower gets a bonus when the enemy fielded no wall break to strip its cover.

lastPickSpecialist._comment: A brawler with a thin map sample is a niche option. This USED to lift entirely at slots 5-6 on the theory that niche picks are last-pick picks — but combined with counters peaking at slot 6 that is exactly how a 41-map-game brawler reached the top of the list. A thin sample is a demerit at every slot now; the last pick gets its own presence floor on top (see mapPriority.lastPick).

throwerLastPick._counterPairNote: The class gate above is not sufficient on its own, because a class cell describes CLASSES and not two brawlers. BOLT is the single best thrower counter in the game at +12.27 win-rate points over 1,964 pairings - and he is a TANK, whose class cell against THROWER is -0.04, so the class check waves him straight through. Same for SHELLY (Anti-Tank, +5.71), BROCK (Sniper, +5.55), ASH (Tank, +4.99) and GRAY (Support, +3.68): five of the fourteen strongest thrower counters are not space makers. So the window also closes when a REVEALED enemy brawler's measured shrunk edge over this thrower reaches this many win-rate points. Set to mapPairs.chipEdgePts so the window can never contradict a chip on its own card: if the card would say 'Loses to their Bolt', the window must not also say the thrower is uncontested. Verified: before this the window fired against Bolt and Shelly and suppressed only for class-level space makers.
throwerLastPick._counterNote: The last-pick window is about COUNTER-DRAFT risk being over, not a licence to throw into a comp that already answers throwers. It now requires that no REVEALED enemy class beats THROWER on the measured counterMatrix by at least this many win-rate points. Read from the matrix rather than a hand-listed class so it follows the data: today only SPACE_MAKER clears 1.0 (+2.06 vs THROWER, the largest cell in the matrix). That matches the measurement exactly - across 332,172 Masters games a thrower is +2.89 win-rate points against a comp with no space maker, -2.06 against one, -4.73 against two and -8.66 against three, a clean monotone dose-response. Before this gate the bonus and its 'Thrower window' chip fired regardless, so a card could read 'Thrower window' beside 'Loses to their Kenji' with three space makers on the board. NOTE the magnitude of the counter effect is already carried by the class matrix (-2.06 x classCounter.adviceWeight 2.0 per space maker, which lands within a point of the measured dose-response) - do NOT add a second explicit penalty here or it will be double counted. Verified: at last pick Barley ranks 4th into a comp with no space maker and 57th into three.
throwerLastPick.label: Thrower window

denial._comment: Interception drafting: the engine evaluates the ENEMY's theoretical best next pick; if that brawler also scores well for us, stealing it denies their plan.
denial.label: Denies their pick

mapProfiles._comment: Ranked pool geometry (owner-provided draft doc, 2026-07-20; Crystal Arcade + Deathcap Trap replaced Rustic Arcade on the 2026-07-22 rotation). openness: OPEN boosts long range / penalizes short; CLOSED the reverse (+throwers, who want walls); MIXED neutral. bushDensity HIGH/MEDIUM feeds the bushSynergy bonus. Entries flagged _estimated are Claude's read of the map rather than owner-confirmed — correct them if they play differently. Keys are canonical DB map names; the engine matches them case- and punctuation-insensitively (lookupByMap), so the duplicated apostrophe/case variants below are belt-and-suspenders only. Maps absent here get no geometry modifiers.

brawlerAttributes._comment: Mechanical facts per brawler: range (Short/Mid/Long), attackType (SINGLE_SHOT/BURST/SPREAD/PIERCE/SPLASH), spawner (true only for ATTACKABLE summons that soak single shots — 8-Bit's booster, Nani's Peep, Bea's goo and Sprout's hedge deliberately excluded), bushSynergy (invisibility/bush-vision/ambush kits), scaler (late-game power spikes — two on one team lose the early map). Sourced from the owner's draft docs (2026-07-20 roster expansion included) with corrections; classes in those docs are IGNORED — brawlerClassOverrides is the class authority.

attributeRules._comment: Mechanical interaction rules from the draft doc, magnitudes retuned to this engine's ~50-point score scale (the doc's raw ±15-20% would swamp real win-rate edges, where 5% WR = 2.5 pts). Geometry modifiers are DAMPENED by dampWithMapData when the brawler has a solid map sample — the live map WR already encodes how the map treats them, so the static prior mainly fills in when data is thin.

singleShotVsSpawner._comment: High-damage single instances get eaten by attackable summons. Waived when a teammate brings PIERCE/SPLASH wave-clear.
singleShotVsSpawner._measuredNote: scoreMultiplier 0.88 (about -6 points on the ~50-point base) replaced by penaltyPts -0.3, the measured 2x2 interaction: SINGLE_SHOT against an enemy spawner is -0.31 +/- 0.31, i.e. real in direction but a twentieth of what was shipped. BOUNCE joins the waiver list because a bouncing shot clears summons the same way pierce and splash do.
singleShotVsSpawner.label: Summon fodder

clearsSummons._comment: Pierce/splash clears summons while still hitting the primary target.
clearsSummons._measuredNote: PIERCE 5 -> 0.9 and SPLASH 3 -> 0.4, from the measured 2x2 interaction over 3.0M Masters sides: (win rate with this attack type AND an enemy spawner, minus without the type) minus the same difference when the enemy has no spawner, so the brawler's own strength cannot masquerade as a spawner interaction. PIERCE measured +0.93 +/- 0.31 and SPLASH +0.36 +/- 0.31 against shipped constants of +5 and +3. BOUNCE added 2026-08-31 for Jessie, whose shot bounces off a target rather than piercing - owner-confirmed that it clears summons, so it takes PIERCE's value; it is NOT separately measured, since it is one brawler.
clearsSummons.label: Clears summons

geometry._comment: wallBreakShiftsOpen: a friendly wall breaker physically opens the map mid-game — CLOSED evaluates as MIXED, MIXED as OPEN (dynamic map mutation).
geometry._pendingRescaleNote: THESE MULTIPLIERS ARE MEASURED WRONG BY 4-9x AND ARE STILL SHIPPED. Long spans 11 points (OPEN x1.10 vs CLOSED x0.88 on a ~50-point base) and Short spans 12.5, while the measured spreads are 2.58 +/- 0.34 and 1.37 +/- 0.34. The direction is right and monotone across all three openness levels - long-range lift is +0.02 on OPEN maps, -1.16 on MIXED, -2.56 on CLOSED, and short range mirrors it at +0.60 / +1.57 / +1.97 - so the fix is a rescale to additive points (OPEN Long +1.3 / Short -0.7, CLOSED Long -1.3 / Short +0.7, MIXED neutral), not a retraction. It is held back from the 2026-08-31 schema commit deliberately: on 54 real draft states the rescale moves 8 of 54 top picks, because dropping the OPEN x0.85 hands every short-range brawler about +7 points on an open map. That is a correct correction but not a small one, so it wants its own commit and its own look. The CLOSED THROWER x1.08 should go to 0 at the same time - throwers measure -2.40 on closed maps against -0.11 on open, the opposite sign, but that reading is confounded by mode (the closed set skews to gemGrab and heist, throwers' two worst modes at -5.37 and -3.45), so there is no evidence for the bonus and not enough to invert it.

wallBreakOwnThrower._comment: Anti-synergy: a friendly wall breaker destroys the cover the team's own thrower depends on. Applied in both directions (wall breaker joining a thrower comp, or thrower joining a wall-break comp). Exempt in Heist, where breaking the safe lane open is the whole point.
wallBreakOwnThrower._measuredNote: scoreMultiplier 0.92 replaced by penaltyPts 0 on 2026-08-31. The claim is that a friendly wall breaker strips your own thrower's cover. Measured on the OLD (wrong) tag set it came out +1.61, i.e. backwards - but that reading is confounded, because the tagged brawlers were mostly strong ones (Brock, Stu, Griff), so 'thrower plus a strong brawler' beat 'thrower alone' for reasons that have nothing to do with cover. Set to 0 rather than inverted: there is no evidence for the shipped penalty and not enough for its opposite. Re-measure on the corrected tag list before restoring a value.
wallBreakOwnThrower.label: Breaks own cover

scalerSaturation._comment: Two late-game scaling kits on one team concede the early map. Applies to brawlers flagged scaler in brawlerAttributes.
scalerSaturation.label: Second scaler

utilitySaturation._comment: In DPS-hungry objective modes, a third pick from the utility classes loses the damage race (mode classWeights already discourage one; this catches the mixed-class trio the duplicate penalty misses).
utilitySaturation.label: Third utility pick

mapRules._comment: Per-map competitive requirements from pro map breakdowns (SpenLC, 2026-07-22), layered ON TOP of the statistical core rather than replacing it. Every multiplier here is a PRIOR: dampWithMapData shrinks it toward 1.0 when the candidate has a real sample on this map, because the live map win rate already encodes whatever the pro is describing — the prior mainly carries the maps and brawlers where data is still thin. Primitives: penalizeClasses / favorClasses / favorBrawlers (flat multipliers); penaltyExemptSlots (a class penalty that lifts at the named pick slots, e.g. snipers are fine as the 6th pick); requireTeamAbility (a class stays handicapped until the TEAM fields an enabling ability); conditionalPenalty (class penalty waived by a teammate class); requireArchetype (comp mandate — candidates that do NOT satisfy it are penalized once the team is running out of slots to satisfy it, ramping in as the last pick approaches, since a flat whole-team penalty would not change any ranking); wallBreakBonus (multiplier for WALL_BREAK ability holders); banSuggestions and note (advisory only, surfaced in the UI, never scored). Map keys are matched case- and punctuation-insensitively, so 'Belles Rock' and "Belle's Rock" both resolve.

Dry Season.note: Surge, 8-Bit and Meg lead here. Max answers snipers — watch for Sprout / Kit / Bolt on their last pick.

Hideout.note: Ban Brock, then first-pick Surge. Pearl punishes Max and aggressive divers.

Layer Cake.note: No snipers early — take mid control plus one aggro opener, and leave snipers for the last pick.

Shooting Star.note: Surge jumps mid for kills. Dual ranged (Belle / Byron / Brock / Piper) with Jae-Yong for the blue star.

Center Stage.note: Griff-led DPS map. Max / Damian / 8-Bit / Rico dominate; pure dive assassins struggle into that much damage.

Pinball Dreams.note: Needs one aggressive pusher (Shade / Damian / Kenji) plus a mid poke (Max / 8-Bit / Otis / Lumi / Rico).

Sneaky Fields.note: Mid flex pinchers (Rico / Ruffs / Max / Meeple). Pair any utility pick with heavy DPS or their 6th pick punishes you.

Triple Dribble.note: Lane pinchers (Meeple / Moe / Lumi) win the sides; Kenji / Edgar / Mina pressure down the right wall.

Double Swoosh.note: Run vision gear here. Right lane goes aggro onto their carrier, left lane plays a safe defender.

Hard Rock Mine.note: Max is the premier carrier — Pearl / Lola / Crow answer him. Save the last pick for a space-making assassin.

Gem Fort.note: Burst and team wipes decide it — bring mid sustain, a bush scout, and a sneaky assassin/tank (or Sandy) for carrier kills.

Undermine.note: Messy map — you always want an assassin or pressure pick (Alli) to rob the gem carrier.

Crystal Arcade.note: Break both lanes open inside 40 seconds and low-range enemy comps collapse. Safe carriers: Stu / Max / Meg / Pearl.

Deathcap Trap.note: Right lane defensive pincher (Ruffs / Rico), left lane aggro into the grass pocket. Penny is a strong late pick.

Bridge Too Far.note: At most one defender. Surge and Starr Nova win the 1v1s; keep one safe DPS (Colt / Brock / 8-Bit / Amber).

Hot Potato.note: Defensive anchor (Lumi / Meeple) plus a high-DPS follow-up; Carl and Melodie force map control.

Kaboom Canyon.note: Won on defence-to-offence transitions — don't over-draft snipers.

Safe Zone.note: Penny is the premier, near-uncounterable pick. Mid plays range/defence, the sides bring high DPS (Colt / Penny).

Dueling Beetles.note: Griff and Lou lead. Ban Gray to kill the Gray + Emz cheese.

Open Business.note: Pure controller map: one controller, one DPS, one heavy zone sitter. Aggro struggles without a tank holding the zone.

Parallel Plays.note: Split the roles: one peeking defender (Charlie / R-T / Willow / Emz), one wall-jumping attacker (Shade / Damian), one zone pincher.

Ring of Fire.note: Raw-DPS meta — late assassins struggle here. Crow / Lumi / Griff / Finx / Glowy / Poco lead.

Belle's Rock.note: Rico dominates and Brock is his answer. You need at least one high-health pressure anchor.

Flaring Phoenix.note: Mid wants a sniper (Gene / Piper / Mandy), left a thrower or assassin (Squeak / Gray); Buster and Ollie play the poison gas well.

New Horizons.note: Back-wall camping decides this map — bring wall break or pierce, or your snipers get turtled out of the game.

requireTeamAbility.label: No wall break for your sniper

Out in the Open.note: Break the back wall or you get spawn-trapped. Balance DPS with enough range that you aren't out-ranged.

brawlerBias._comment: Pro-source tier corrections (SpenLC, 2026-07-22) for balance changes the patch aggregate has not fully priced in yet. Deliberately small (<=1.08) and damped by dampWithRecentData once the brawler has a solid RECENT sample — a live star-power rework is exactly what the 14-day recency window in statisticalCoefficients already detects, so this prior only has to cover the lag before that sample fills. Keyed by mode; a bias entry with no matching mode key contributes nothing.
brawlerBias._emptyNote: EMPTY as of 2026-08-31, deliberately - the mechanism is kept, the three entries were removed after measurement. The block exists to price a balance change the aggregate has not caught up with yet, but all three entries were describing strength the aggregate had ALREADY priced, so they double counted the score base. The engine scores on blendMapGlobal, which is the brawler's own win rate on this map blended toward their MODE rate - so a mode-keyed multiplier adds a second copy of exactly that. Measured mode win rate vs the brawler's own global: BROCK bounty 54.59 vs 51.27 and knockout 56.37 vs 51.27 (both genuinely strong, both already in the base), SURGE gemGrab 51.01 vs 49.76 and bounty 50.82 vs 49.76, GRIFF hotZone 52.07 vs 50.39. GRIFF brawlBall was outright wrong at 50.20 against his own 50.39 global - the entry paid about +4 points to a brawler performing slightly BELOW his average there. If a real balance change lands mid-patch, the 14-day recency window in statisticalCoefficients is the mechanism built to catch it; use this block only for the lag before that window fills, and never for a brawler whose mode record already shows the strength.

brawlerCounters._comment: Named brawler-vs-brawler multipliers from pro sources. Sits ABOVE the class counter matrix (which would only see Control vs Support) and BELOW empirical vs_brawler data — when a pair has 100+ real games, PASS 2 has already priced the matchup and this prior is damped the same way every other prior is.
brawlerCounters._emptyNote: EMPTY as of 2026-08-31, deliberately. The single entry - PEARL x1.25 vs MAX, KIT and MORTIS - was measured against vs_brawler and two thirds of it was false. Pearl's own global is 51.85%%; she is 51.27%% vs MAX over 22,922 games and 51.32%% vs MORTIS over 7,165, i.e. very slightly WORSE than her own average against both, while the rule paid about +12 points. Only KIT holds, at 56.29%% over 1,949 games (+4.44 relative) - and that pairing is already in the score at mapPairs.suggestWeight 1.8, so the multiplier was a second copy of a number the engine measures directly. That is the general rule for this block: it exists for pairings vs_brawler CANNOT see (too few games), so an entry that clears pairMinPicks does not belong here. Add future entries as points, damped by map data, never as a multiplier.

firstPickCaution._comment: Named pro caveat for a brawler that is strong on a map but exploitable as an early reveal. EMPTY as of 2026-08-30, deliberately. It held one entry - BROCK, x0.85 on slots 1-2, waived if MAX was banned - and every part of it failed a check. The waiver encoded a counter that does not exist: Max vs Brock measures 49.81% over 37,243 games, one of the largest samples in vs_brawler, so banning Max was worth nothing to Brock while the rule handed him about +5 points. Brock's real answers, weighted by how likely the enemy is to pick them, are Stu, Meg and Ash. The penalty itself duplicated the counterability term, which now covers 'exploitable as an early reveal' for every brawler and scales with enemyPicksRemaining. And its multiplicative form broke the scale contract in `scoring`. If a genuine named caveat comes up, add it as penaltyPts (win-rate points, damped by map data) - never as a multiplier, and never with a hand-listed ban waiver, because banRelief answers that from measured pairings.

winProbability._comment: Draft-complete win split. Logistic squash of the comp-score differential; capped 85/15 because no draft is ever truly 90-10 — execution still exists.
winProbability._logisticScaleNote: 33.5 -> 35.0 on 2026-08-30, a PROPORTIONAL adjustment rather than a fit. The verdict's base changed that day - blendMapGlobal now shrinks a thin map reading toward the brawler's MODE rate instead of their global rate - which widened the comp-score differential by 4.45%% (sd 8.690 -> 9.076 over 720 random full drafts). logisticScale encodes how wide that differential runs, so leaving it at 33.5 would have made every verdict correspondingly overconfident. Scaling it by the same 1.0445 preserves the calibration the last real fit established. The win split moved by >=1pp in 415 of 720 drafts, largest change 5pp. THIS IS INTERIM: the weekly calibration job (Mondays 04:40 UTC, scripts/calibrate.mjs) refits the scale against real outcomes and should be treated as authoritative over this number. The job already guards the risk - it exits non-zero if the shipped scale drifts more than 50%% from the fitted one or if a calibration bucket is off by more than 5pp, and a 4.45%% move is far inside both.
winProbability._counterWeightComment: Per-point weight of the class counter matrix in each side's comp score. MUST stay at half the intuitive value: counterMatrix is exactly antisymmetric (M[a][b] === -M[b][a]), so red's counter total is always the negation of blue's, and the differential blue-minus-red therefore counts every cross-team pairing TWICE. At the old 1.2 this let class theory swing the differential by up to ~26 points while the statistical term (a mean of true win rates) spans barely 6 — i.e. the matrix outvoted real win-rate evidence roughly 4:1, and could hand a 67% verdict to the comp with the WORSE measured win rates. 0.6 counts each pairing once, which puts theory and evidence on comparable footing and keeps the split consistent with the suggestion ranking.
winProbability._calibration: counterWeight 0 and logisticScale 33.5 are MEASURED, not chosen, and the scale must be REFITTED whenever a scoring term is added or removed — it encodes how wide the differential runs. Backtested on 35,257 games played after a training cutoff with every aggregate rebuilt from matches collected before it. At the original 0.6/14 the verdict scored WORSE than always saying 50/50 (logloss 0.6984 vs 0.6931) and claimed 70% where teams actually won 58.8%. Ablation: the class counter matrix COST ranking power here (0.5587 -> 0.5622 without it) while the head-to-head vs_brawler term earned its place (-0.0138 without it) at a near-optimal 0.6. Adding measured duo synergy took it further. Now AUC 0.5734, logloss 0.6846, Brier 0.2458 — all better than a coin flip, every calibration bucket within 1.8pp. The matrix is UNCHANGED in getDraftAdvice, where it is weighted 2.2x and drives the Counters/Weak-vs chips.

mapPairs._comment: Measured brawler-vs-brawler win rates from brawler_intelligence.vs_brawler — the counter-drafting evidence for the late picks: 'does this candidate actually beat the brawlers they are looking at'. Named mapPairs because a per-map layer slots in here later; today the numbers are patch-wide, and the engine reads them through pairEdgeVs in draftEngine.js. Worth knowing why per-map is a second-order refinement rather than the main event: the measured spread of a pair's true edge is ~4.3 win-rate points, while the spread of the MAP-SPECIFIC part of that edge is only ~2.3, so the patch-wide rate is the trunk and the map rate is a correction to it.
mapPairs._mapShrinkNote: Shrink prior for the PER-MAP head-to-head layer (map_pair_edges), blending a pair's record on this map toward its patch-wide rate. Live since 2026-08-30 and the largest single gain the calibration pass has produced: +0.0043 +/-0.0029 AUC on 23,772 held-out pick decisions, beating the +0.0032 from refitting every recommender weight at once. Deliberately smaller than the patch-wide 135: validation preferred the smallest prior tried (50) and the curve is monotone in that direction, so the map layer wants MORE weight rather than less. The long tail is not stored - of 169,191 per-map pairings only 18.7%% reach 30 games and 2.6%% reach 200 - so anything below the RPC floor falls straight through to the patch-wide rate, which is the same thing shrinkage would have done to it anyway. Antisymmetry survives: both directions are stored, so mapWR(a,b) = 100 - mapWR(b,a) and the blend weight is identical either way.
mapPairs._shrinkComment: Empirical-Bayes shrink of a pair edge toward even. prior = 2500/sd^2, where 2500 is the squared standard error of a win rate (50/sqrt(n)) and sd is the measured spread of a pair's true edge vs 50%: 4.3 points, stable across every sample bucket from 50 games to 1000+. So a 30-game pair contributes 18% of its raw edge, a 300-game pair 69%, a 3,000-game pair 96%. This REPLACED a hard picks>=100 step gate, under which a 99-game pair counted for nothing and a 100-game pair for everything.
mapPairs._suggestComment: Weight of the mean head-to-head edge in getDraftAdvice's candidate score, further scaled by counterLadder.counterWeightBySlot so it matters most at the late picks. Was a hardcoded 0.8 alongside the step gate.
mapPairs._splitComment: Weight of the same term in computeWinSplit. MUST stay half the intuitive value, for exactly the winProbability.counterWeight reason: pairEdgeVs is antisymmetric (vs_brawler is built from the same matches for both directions), so red's total is the negation of blue's and the blue-minus-red differential counts every pairing TWICE. Note also that the term is a MEAN over the 9 cross-team pairings, not a sum — a sum would let one brawler's three favourable matchups swing the verdict ~20 points through logisticScale, which is the same class of error as counterWeight at 1.2. Setting this and suggestWeight to 0 disables the whole feature in both code paths with no code change.
mapPairs._chipComment: Thresholds on the SHRUNK edge, not the raw win rate, so a thin fluke can never produce a 'Beats their X' chip or headline a note.
mapPairs._noteMinGamesComment: A SINGLE pairing must clear this before its raw win rate may headline a card. Shrinkage governs the score, but the note prints the unshrunk figure, and '58.3% vs their El Primo · 60 games' is the same noise-dressed-as-evidence problem mapPriority.headlineMinMapPicks solves for map rates. 300 matches the floor the brawler-guide Match-ups section uses for the same data. The comp-level note is deliberately exempt — it averages across the enemy team rather than reading one thin duel as fact.
mapPairs._suggestWeightNote: 1.0 -> 1.8 on 2026-08-29. This is the RECOMMENDER's head-to-head weight; computeWinSplit's splitWeight is deliberately left alone because changing a verdict scoring term invalidates the fitted logisticScale and needs a refit through the calibration job. Validated on held-out games rather than on a proxy: a validation sweep rises 0.5470 / 0.5476 / 0.5479 across 1.0 / 1.4 / 1.8 and then flattens through 3.2, and 1.8 is the conservative end of that plateau. On its own the raise is +0.0010 +/-0.0011 (not significant); paired with duoSynergy.adviceWeight 1.6 the two together are +0.0032 +/-0.0011 held out, which is significant. Deleting the head-to-head term entirely costs -0.0075 +/-0.0030, the largest single term in the recommender. vs_brawler is the best-evidenced signal we have: 93% of real pick decisions involve enemy pairings with 200+ games of direct data, and 68% have over a thousand.

mapPriority._comment: How hard the engine leans on THIS MAP's data versus the brawler's overall patch numbers. The old behaviour was a fixed 65/35 map/overall blend that applied only when the map sample cleared minMapPicks — and a brawler with NO map data silently fell through to a pure overall score, so 'unproven here' scored identically to 'proven here'. blendPriorGames replaces that with sample weighting: map weight = mapPicks / (mapPicks + blendPriorGames), so weight rises smoothly with evidence and is 0 when there is none.

presenceFloor._comment: Brawlers below minPresencePct of this map's games are pushed behind everything that clears the bar, on the EARLY picks only. It lifts for slots 5 and 6, where a niche answer is exactly the point: the enemy comp is essentially set by then and a specialist counter can no longer be counter-drafted. Same slot list as throwerPenalty, for the same reason. Owner decision 2026-08-30: 'just because they picked Brock there shouldn't be an automatic Ash pick in bounty'. THIS IS A PREFERENCE, NOT A MEASURED IMPROVEMENT, and the price is known and was shown before it was chosen. Floors were tested four ways over 23,772 held-out decisions and every one lost: presence 1%% -0.0091, presence 3%% -0.0102, presence 15%% -0.0230, min-50-map-games -0.0077, min-200 -0.0101, graded 400-early-to-0-late -0.0042; a 5%% floor sits near -0.0126, all significant. The reason is that rare picks are not bad picks - the picks real Masters players made below 1%% presence won 51.6%%, below 15%% presence 50.2%% - and a floor cannot tell the two cases apart: on Dry Season it removes Ash (0.56%% presence, 396 games, 58.1%% on the map) along with Amber (0.20%%, 144 games, 47.2%%). Set minPresencePct to 0 to disable. It never shortens the list: brawlers below the floor are appended behind those above it, not deleted.

orderByWinRate._comment: First pick only. Takes the poolSize most-PLAYED brawlers on this map and orders exactly those by win rate — at 7 the list is literally 'the seven most-picked here, best win rate first', which is what the owner asked for after seeing it as a column (Gem Fort: Stu 52.8, Rico 51.7, Mortis 51.6, Surge 51.4, Griff 50.8, Max 50.1, Meg 49.2). Nothing outside that seven can appear however well it performs: on Gem Fort, Bolt is 59.6% over 5,852 games but only the 27th most-picked, so he is absent at poolSize 7 and 20 and leads the list at 30. That is the single knob for the trade-off. It is a PRESENTATION rule for slot 1, not an accuracy improvement, and the difference is deliberate: a use-rate term inside the SCORE was tested in three shapes (linear, log, sqrt) at six weights each and every combination lost on 23,772 held-out decisions (-0.0007 to -0.0021, all significant, monotone in weight), as did presence used as a floor (-0.0012). Popularity measures what players pick, not what wins — across six maps only 27 of 42 most-picked brawlers were above 50%, and the most-picked brawler measured (Colt, 49.1% of games on Hot Potato) sits at exactly 49.1%. So presence chooses the POOL and win rate does the ordering; presence adds no points anywhere in the engine. Ordering uses the same blended rate the card displays, so the list and the card can never disagree.
orderByWinRate._exceptionalNote: A brawler outside the most-picked pool still gets in if it is winning this hard on a real sample. Nori is 62.1% over 8,671 games on Hot Potato and only the 17th most-picked there - 'nobody has caught on yet' is not a reason to hide her. Gated on the SHRUNK win rate (trueWR) plus a presence floor rather than a raw threshold, because a flat cut is brittle in both directions: it would admit a 200-game fluke at 62% and drop a 59.9% staple. Shrinkage barely touches a four-figure sample (Nori 62.1 raw vs 62.0 shrunk) and pulls a thin one hard toward even, so the guard costs nothing where the evidence is real. sampleScope must be 'map' - an overall rate standing in for a missing map read must never trigger this. Calibrated on six mode-representative maps: at 57 it admits four brawlers in total (Nori 62.1, Bolt 59.6 and 58.7 on two maps, Bibi 57.7); at 60 it would admit only Nori; at 55 it admits nine and starts to drown the most-picked character of the list.

firstPick._comment: First pick is a map question before it is a matchup question: with no enemy revealed, the only real evidence is whether a brawler wins AND is actually played on this map. presencePct = share of this map's matches the brawler appears in (sums to ~600% across the pool, so an even split over ~105 brawlers is ~5.7%).

mapPriority._headlineComment: A map win rate only HEADLINES a suggestion card once the sample can carry it. minMapPicks (30) is the floor for a map rate to enter SCORING at all, where the Bayesian shrink in trueWR keeps it honest — but the card shows a raw wins/picks figure, and 41 games rendering as a confident '53.7%' map read is noise dressed as evidence. Below this the card headlines the overall rate instead and still prints the map sample beside it.

lastPick._comment: The last pick is ranked by the win split it produces, so none of the score multipliers below reach it — which let class theory drag in brawlers with a 0.1% presence on the map purely because they countered a class. A pro's last pick is a counter to the enemy comp that is ALSO a real pick on the map, so candidates must clear a presence floor before they are ranked. If fewer than minCandidates survive (thin map data, heavy bans), the floor is dropped rather than returning nothing. At 1.5% this leaves 46-66 eligible brawlers per map.

mapPriority._blendPriorNote: LEFT AT 400 on purpose. Validation mildly preferred 150-200, but the held-out difference across 60/100/150/200/300/400 is under 0.0008 AUC with a paired margin covering zero at every value. It also is NOT recommender-only: computeWinSplit's strength() calls blendMapGlobal too, so moving it perturbs the verdict differential and would invalidate the fitted logisticScale (33.5). WHAT THE BLEND SHRINKS TOWARD changed on 2026-08-30: the fallback is now the brawler's rate in this MODE (see modeFallbackMinPicks) and only their global rate when the mode sample is thin. A record in gem grab is a better prior for a gem grab map than one pooled across heist and bounty; Bolt is 59.6% on Gem Fort against 55.1% global, so shrinking toward global dragged a well-measured map reading toward modes he is barely played in. Measured +0.0009 +/-0.0008 AUC on 23,772 held-out decisions - small, only just clear of its bar, but the right sign and a fair like-for-like comparison. CORRECTION: an earlier version of this note claimed shrinking toward 50%% instead 'cost 0.0039 AUC'. That does not reproduce - on the same harness shrinking toward 50%% SCORES BETTER (+0.0012), and removing the win-rate base entirely scores better still (+0.0023), which is nonsense as advice. That harness scores one pick against its own team's result, so terms differentiating the two teams are priced correctly while a brawler's standalone strength largely cancels out of the outcome. It can compare variants of the base against each other; it cannot price the base against nothing. Do not use it to argue for weakening the win-rate term.

banStrategy._comment: Who you ban depends entirely on whether you pick FIRST or LAST, and the old list ignored that — it just showed the six strongest brawlers on the map to both teams. That is actively wrong for the first-pick team: banning the best brawler in the game when you hold first pick throws the ban away, because you could simply have taken him. First pick => you get the best opener, so what you cannot control is their LAST pick answering your revealed comp. Ban the counter-pick threats. Last pick => they will open on the best brawler and you will never see him. Ban the meta openers to deny them. firstPickSafety (draftMeta) is the discriminator: high = safe to reveal early, so that's who gets first-picked; low = wins come from favourable matchups, so that's a last-pick counter threat.
banStrategy._presenceComment: Same floor as mapPriority.lastPick — a brawler nobody plays on this map is not worth a ban.

denyOpeners._comment: For the team picking LAST: rank the meta openers the enemy would first-pick. Mild tilt toward takeable-first brawlers, kept mild so a genuinely broken low-safety brawler still surfaces.
denyOpeners.headline: They pick first — deny the openers
denyOpeners.reason: Meta opener — they take this if you don't ban it

protectFromCounters._comment: For the team picking FIRST: rank the last-pick counter threats. skipTopOpeners removes the brawlers this team would realistically open on — banning your own first pick is the exact mistake this rule exists to prevent.
protectFromCounters.headline: You pick first — ban their counter-picks
protectFromCounters.reason: Last-pick threat — answers your comp after you reveal
protectFromCounters._maxOpenerComment: Hard exclusion, not just a weighting. At firstPickSafety >= this a brawler is a SAFE OPENER (same threshold blindPickLabel uses for that badge) — which means the team holding first pick can simply take them. Banning your own first pick is the specific mistake this whole rule exists to prevent, so those are removed from the first-picker's ban list outright rather than merely down-weighted.

banStrategy.proBanReason: Pro priority ban on this map

duoSynergy._comment: MEASURED teammate synergy, replacing the hand-authored synergyPairs table. Hold-out validated 2026-08-27: weight fitted on half of 35,257 post-cutoff games and scored on the other half, AUC 0.5662 -> 0.5764 (+0.0102) — the largest single gain of the whole calibration pass. The signal is the EXCESS over what the two brawlers' solo rates already predict, not the raw duo win rate: raw conflates synergy with individual strength, so two strong brawlers look synergistic with no interaction at all. Raw scored +0.0088 held out, excess +0.0102. Real measured duos: Colt+Nori +12.0pp, Emz+Damian +5.7pp over 3,483 games, while Gene+Max is +0.1pp over 11,951 — a pairing that feels synergistic and measurably is not.
duoSynergy._adviceWeightNote: 1.0 -> 1.6 on 2026-08-29, and unlike the old value this one IS validated against outcomes. Fitted on a validation half of 48,306 post-cutoff games and confirmed once on the other half: together with suggestWeight 1.8 it moves recommendation AUC +0.0032 with a DeLong paired 95% margin of +/-0.0011, the only change in this pass that clears its own error bar. Measured on its own, deleting the duo term costs -0.0030 +/-0.0012, so it is carrying real signal and was underweighted. The validation surface is a plateau from ~1.4 through 2.4; 1.6 is its interior rather than its edge, because the grid maximum (2.4, at the boundary of what was swept) is the value most likely to be fitting noise. Note this is the RECOMMENDER weight - duoSynergy.weight (2.4) is the separate verdict term and must not be moved without a logisticScale refit. Still the excess over the pair's solo rates, never the raw duo rate.

classCounter._comment: How the class counter matrix enters getDraftAdvice. It is now a MEASURED matrix in win-rate points, not the authored -2..+2 table, so both numbers here changed together and neither is comparable to its old value. adviceWeight 0.8 -> 2.0 is a UNIT CONVERSION, not a promotion: the measured matrix has RMS 0.88 where the authored one had 1.21, and 2.0 keeps the term's contribution to the score roughly where 1.4 put the old one - which is where a validation sweep peaked, on a curve that is flat from 0 through 4.0. Be clear about what this term is worth: held out over 23,772 real pick decisions, going from the authored matrix to the measured one moved AUC +0.0002 +/-0.0013, and removing the class matrix ALTOGETHER moved it -0.0008 +/-0.0010. None of those clear their error bars. A class matrix cannot add much once brawler-level vs_brawler is present, which covers 93% of real decisions - that is the finding, and it has now been reproduced three times (authored values, measured values, and 18 learned classes from co-clustering). It is kept non-zero because it drives every 'Counters X' / 'Weak vs Y' chip and the counterStack rule, and those explanations are worth more when they are true than the ranking is worth when they are absent.
classCounter._adviceWeightRevision: 2.0 -> 0.6 on 2026-08-30. This term buys NO ranking accuracy - removing the class matrix entirely moves AUC by -0.0008 +/-0.0010 and every weight from 0 to 4.0 is statistically identical - but it was actively producing bad lists. On Center Stage at pick 5 against Emz (Anti-Tank) it handed every thrower +1.71 x 2.0 = +3.4 while charging Bolt -1.06 x 2.0, a ~6 point swing that put Sirius (47.2%% on the map) and Sprout (46.6%%) third and fourth ahead of Rosa (54.9%%) and Stu. At 0.6 that cluster disappears and Rosa and Stu take their place. CHIPS ARE UNAFFECTED: 'Counters X' / 'Weak vs Y' fire off the raw cell against classCounter.chipThreshold, and counterStack reads matrixScore directly, so the explanations the matrix exists for all survive. This is the term's stated purpose - it explains picks, it does not rank them - now reflected in its weight.
classCounter._deferNote: The class matrix stops emitting a chip about a specific pairing once the MEASUREMENT can speak for it - either it has this many games of vs_brawler data, or its shrunk edge already clears mapPairs.chipEdgePts so the 'Beats their X' / 'Loses to their X' chip will fire. Both conditions are needed: a games-only gate still let a ~150-game pairing chip on edge and collide. WHY: a class cell describes CLASSES, not two brawlers, and within-class spread dwarfs the class mean - against throwers Bolt is +5.79 and Buster -5.19 around a class mean of ~0. Without the gate the two chip sources contradicted each other on the same card, e.g. 'Weak vs Emz' (Tank vs Anti-Tank, -1.06) beside 'Beats their Emz' (measured 54.9% over 1,341 games, and the correct one). Measured over 4,764 scored cards: contradictions ran 4.72% under the old authored matrix, 2.48% once it was measured, and 0.00% with this gate. 200 matches the shrinkage floor used elsewhere and the coverage the weighting rests on - 93% of real pick decisions involve pairings with 200+ games - so the class chip now speaks only where vs_brawler genuinely cannot. This gates the CHIP ONLY. Scores are byte-identical: matrixPts accumulates before the skip, deliberately, because the scoring term was measured both as a fallback and as an always-on additive and the two were indistinguishable (0.5462 vs 0.5464), so the simpler additive form was kept.
classCounter._chipThresholdNote: Absolute class edge, in win-rate points, at which the recommender shows a 'Counters X' or 'Weak vs Y' chip. Was hardcoded at 1.5 against the authored -2..+2 scale; on the measured scale (RMS 0.88, max 2.15) that would have left only Space Maker vs Thrower and Thrower vs Anti-Tank able to fire. 1.0 means 'a full win-rate point of class edge' and lights the pairings the data actually supports: Anti-Tank/Tank (+1.07), Space Maker/Thrower (+2.15), Space Maker/Sniper (+1.13), Tank/Space Maker (+1.11), Tank/Control (+1.12), Thrower/Control (+1.14), Thrower/Anti-Tank (+1.66). Raising it makes the engine quieter and more certain; lowering it makes claims the sample cannot carry.

mapClassFit._comment: Weight on MEASURED per-map class fit, read from the map_class_weights table (rebuilt daily by refresh_map_class_weights from meta_weights.py, so it tracks the meta instead of rotting). The value is already in WIN-RATE POINTS - how much a class over/under-performs on that map relative to its own brawlers' global rates, brawler strength removed, then shrunk toward 0 by sample - so weight 1.0 means 'use it at face value' and is the honest default. It is ADDITIVE, replacing the multiplicative modes[].classWeights, and that change is the point: multiplying a 50-90 point score meant CONTROL x1.15 in gemGrab was worth about +11 points, where the effect it described measures at -0.31 on Double Swoosh. MEASURED 2026-08-29 over 23,772 held-out pick decisions: the authored weights cost -0.0041 AUC at shipped strength and -0.0083 at 1.5x - a clean monotone slide, more damage than every improvement made this week combined - while this measured term is NEUTRAL (-0.0000 +/-0.0013). So the gain is from removing a harmful term, not from adding a predictive one. It is largely (not entirely) subsumed by the brawler's own per-map win rate, which the score already carries: turning that off roughly doubles what class fit is worth. Per-map beat per-mode on validation (0.5505 vs 0.5501) but neither cleared its error bar on test. Kept because it is honest, self-refreshing, and drives map-fit explanation.

scoring._comment: THE SCALE CONTRACT. Every scoring term in getDraftAdvice is expressed in WIN-RATE POINTS on a base that is itself a win rate (blendMapGlobal, ~45-60). A term worth N here means 'about N percentage points of win rate'. This exists because the engine used to mix three incompatible scales and the mixture, not any single value, was the bug: multipliers applied to a 50-90 point score (CONTROL x1.15 = about +11 points, blindPickFactor 0.35 = about -40) and flat constants (throwerPenalty -50) both dwarfed every MEASURED term, which run about +/-5-9 points. An influence audit over 60 real draft states found the hand-authored thrower penalty was 30% of all adjustment influence and 62% on early picks, while head-to-head - the term measured as the single largest earner - was 1% there. RULE FOR NEW TERMS: additive, in win-rate points, no multiplier on the running score, and no constant larger than the largest measured term. If a rule needs to be louder than head-to-head, it needs evidence first.
scoring._thinMapFadeNote: What share of the thin-map penalty fades as the enemy runs out of picks. The rest stands for the whole draft. Two things were conflated before: 'they can still answer this' is a counter-draft risk and correctly fades, but 'we do not know whether this brawler works on this map' is a fact about evidence quality that does not stop being true at pick 5. Faded in full, the penalty dropped to a third exactly when the presence floor also lifted, and Larry & Lawrie - 79 games at 40.5%% on Center Stage - topped a pick-5 list twelve points above Bolt at 1,674 games and 54.7%%, on a map whose measured class fit puts THROWER second-worst (-0.67) and TANK best (+1.08). At 0.5 the penalty is full strength on the first pick and half strength on the last. The presence floor is unaffected and still lifts entirely from pick 5.
scoring._thinMapNote: Penalty for a brawler with little evidence ON THIS MAP, scaled by how short of mapPriority.firstPick.headlineMinMapPicks it falls AND by enemyPicksRemaining/3, so it fades to nothing at the last pick. Being unproven here is a COUNTER-DRAFT risk, not a verdict: an Amber first pick can be answered by the three picks still to come, the same Amber taken last into a comp she already counters cannot. A PRIOR, not a fit - pick order is absent from ranked_matches so early-vs-late is unmeasurable, and an earlier attempt to measure it fabricated the order by withholding enemy picks from the scorer, which tests information rather than timing. Kept at 8 against counterability's 14 for that reason. What IS measured is that a flat FLOOR is wrong in every form tried: presence floors 1-15%% cost -0.0091 to -0.0230 and map-game floors 50-800 cost -0.0077 to -0.0158, all significant on 23,772 held-out decisions, because rare picks are not bad picks (51.6%% below 1%% presence) and no floor separates Ash on Dry Season (396 games, 58.1%%) from Amber (144 games, 47.2%%). A graded fading penalty keeps the good rare pick and prices the unproven one.
scoring._counterabilityNote: Maximum points deducted for a fully counterable brawler with all three enemy picks still to come. Replaces `score *= blindPickFactor`, a 0.35-1.0 multiplier that reached about -40 points on an Edgar. Scales with enemyPicksRemaining/3 rather than firing only on an empty board: the risk that the enemy answers your pick lasts as long as they hold picks, which the old binary form ignored the instant they revealed one brawler. The SAFETY values it multiplies stay hand-authored in draftMeta.js - see the note on the counterability block in draftEngine.js for the two failed attempts to derive them and why the data cannot support it.

banRelief._comment: Credit for bans that removed an answer to the candidate. Gated on enemyPicksRemaining, since a ban is only worth something while the enemy could still have used it, and weighted by how likely they were to pick it (map presence): banning Ash removes a bigger per-game threat to Brock, +8.78 pts, than banning Stu at +4.66, but Stu is picked three times as often so the ban removes more real risk. DEDUCTIVE, NOT FITTED - ranked_matches carries no ban data, so there is no hold-out for this and it is entered at its arithmetic value (weight 1.0) rather than tuned. It replaces firstPickCaution.waivedIfBanned, which hard-coded 'Brock is safe once Max is banned'; Max vs Brock measures 49.81% over 37,243 games, so that ban was worth nothing to Brock. The real answers to Brock are Stu, Meg and Ash.

useRate._comment: Small additive nudge toward brawlers this map actually plays, in win-rate points, applied as weight x presence%%. Owner-requested 2026-08-30 on the reasoning that there is a reason a brawler is highly picked. THE SIZE IS THE WHOLE POINT. A use-rate term was measured across three shapes (linear, log, sqrt) and eleven weights on 23,772 held-out decisions and it never once helped; it only stops HURTING when it shrinks to a tie-breaker. Linear 0.10 costs -0.0017 +/-0.0013, 0.05 costs -0.0007 +/-0.0007 (both significant), 0.03 costs -0.0004 +/-0.0004, and 0.02 costs -0.0002 +/-0.0003 - indistinguishable from zero. 0.02 is therefore the largest value that is provably free: about +0.9 points for a 45%%-presence staple against +0.1 for a 5%% niche pick, on a ~50-90 scale. DO NOT RAISE IT past 0.03 without re-measuring; the harm grows monotonically with weight. Why so little: presence already enters the score in the statistically correct way, as CONFIDENCE rather than as a bonus - mapWRk shrinks toward the brawler's global rate by sample size, and on a fixed map games = presence x matches, so on a 70k-match map a 40%%-presence brawler keeps 98.6%% of its map rate while a 3%% one keeps 84%%. The information in popularity is mostly already spent. Popularity is also not a winning signal on its own: across six mode-representative maps only 27 of 42 most-picked brawlers were above 50%%, and the most-picked brawler measured (Colt, in 49.1%% of games on Hot Potato) sits at exactly 49.1%%.
